rationale: Both cover similar technical ground (uncached per-layer kernel fetch, FA3/Blackwell gate vs Hopper-only docs, varlen-func-None residual risk, CI lane/marker gaps) but neither hits the resolved GT threads precisely since the diff already reflects post-fix code. Y is more tightly grounded: nearly every claim quotes exact code plus explains its verification status (validated/claim-refuted), and it independently surfaces the pyproject.toml `kernels<0.15.0` lower-bound gap, which closely matches wtomin's actual ask about minimum kernels version requirements. X raises more findings and reads fluently, but several rest on unverifiable specifics (exact HF commit SHAs, precise cold/warm timing numbers, and a claimed 'kernels 0.16.0' test environment that contradicts the project's own pinned `<0.15.0`), which hurts credibility and precision. Actionability is comparable, with X slightly more readable and Y slightly more evidence-dense.
